modal.inputMethodHelp: Select how audio reaches this input.
modal.fingerprintHelp: Tries to identify track metadata for this input.
modal.sendspinHelp: Stream audio from a Sendspin source client. Capture starts when the input is selected.

The server starts it when the source is picked, stops it when the room moves on, and passes remote buttons through. It sends these to the bridge's on_command hook, so the script on that machine decides what each one does to the hardware. Leave off for a turntable or a plain input — nothing will be sent.

custom.title: Streaming services

When the Loxone role is enabled, each is also exposed as a Spotify-compatible source so the Loxone app can list it.
custom.activeDesc: When the Loxone role is on, each service also appears as its own Spotify-compatible source in the Loxone app.
custom.emptySub: Add a service to make Apple Music, Tidal, Deezer, SoundCloud, YouTube Music or Music Assistant available.

bridge.subtitle: Add a streaming account and choose how to connect it
bridge.providerDesc: Pick which streaming service you want to add.
bridge.nameHelp: Shown in the Loxone app. Give each account a distinct name to tell multiple logins of the same service apart.

ma.desc: Music Assistant exposes one Spotify account per configured MA account. Create dedicated MA accounts with provider filters to surface specific services in Loxone.
ma.connectionDesc: Tell the bridge where to reach your Music Assistant server.
ma.apiKeyHelp: Generate a long-lived token under your Music Assistant account settings.
ma.modeDesc: Choose how Music Assistant integrates with this audio server. You can change this at any time.
ma.sourceDesc: Music Assistant streams audio into this audio server. Each Loxone zone gets a virtual MA player and audio plays through the zone's normal output (sendspin, etc.).
sourceBullets: Audio flows through this server's outputs
Other sources (Spotify Connect, line-in, alerts) keep working alongside MA

ma.sinkDesc: Existing Music Assistant players (Sonos, Chromecast, snapcast, …) appear as Loxone zone outputs. This server only proxies commands and mirrors state.
sinkBullets: No audio passes through this server
Loxone shows live status from MA (now-playing, volume, queue)
Best when MA is already your primary music server

apple.desc: Use a Media User Token from music.apple.com to enable Apple Music browsing and playback. Tokens can be refreshed anytime from your browser session.
apple.tokenDesc: Sign in with Apple to fetch your token automatically, or paste one from your music.apple.com session.
apple.signInHint: Opens an Apple sign-in window and fills the token in for you.
apple.signInPopupBlocked: Could not open the sign-in window. Allow pop-ups and try again.
apple.widevineDesc: Required for Apple Music DRM playback. Stored locally under <1>data/widevine_cdm</1>.
apple.uploadHint: Select private_key.pem and/or client_id.bin before uploading.

ytmusic.desc: YouTube Music signs in with a browser cookie. Copy it from a private browsing window — a cookie taken from a normal tab stops working within the hour, because YouTube replaces it while that tab stays open.
ytmusic.title: Cookie header
ytmusic.descLong: Paste the cookie header from a signed-in music.youtube.com session. Using a private window is the part that makes it last:
ytmusic.step1: Open a private (incognito) window and sign in to music.youtube.com.
ytmusic.step2: Press F12 for developer tools, open Network, and click any request to music.youtube.com.
ytmusic.step3: Under Request Headers, copy everything after "cookie:" and paste it below.
ytmusic.step4: Close the private window without signing out. That keeps YouTube from replacing the cookie you just copied.
ytmusic.potDesc: YouTube keeps its 256 kbps streams for apps that can prove a request came from a real player. That proof comes from a small helper service you run yourself (the bgutil PO Token provider, port 4416 by default). Leave this empty and playback still works, at standard quality.
ytmusic.cookieOk: Cookie works — your library is reachable.
ytmusic.cookieExpired: This cookie is not signed in any more. Paste a fresh one using the steps above.
ytmusic.cookieInvalid: This does not look like a cookie from a signed-in session.
ytmusic.potOff: No helper service set — playing at standard quality.
ytmusic.potPluginMissing: The yt-dlp plugin this needs is not installed yet.

youtube.desc: YouTube works out of the box with no credentials — search and public playlists are available immediately. Add an API key for better search quality.
youtube.callout1: Streams take a few seconds to start.
youtube.callout1Text: YouTube does not expose direct audio URLs — each track is resolved on demand via yt-dlp, which typically takes 3–7 seconds on a cold cache.
youtube.callout2End: immediately, then switches to the track name once audio begins. Subsequent plays are served from a 1-hour cache.
youtube.apiDesc: Enables better search results and trending music charts. Without it, search still works via yt-dlp. Get a free key at <1>Google Cloud Console</1> → Enable "YouTube Data API v3" → Create API key.

deezer.desc: Deezer works without credentials for public catalog data. Add an ARL cookie only if you need private playlists or recommendations.
deezer.title: ARL cookie
deezer.descLong: Add your Deezer ARL cookie to access private playlists or recommendations.

soundcloud.desc: Stream tracks, sets and likes from SoundCloud.
soundcloud.title: OAuth Token (required)
soundcloud.descLong: SoundCloud requires an OAuth token from a logged-in account. Open soundcloud.com in your browser, sign in, then copy the value after 'OAuth ' from the Authorization header of any api-v2 request (DevTools → Network). Note: a minority of tracks are DRM-protected and cannot be played.

tidal.desc: Provide a valid access token plus a two-letter country code to enable Tidal catalog and playback.
tidal.title: Access token
tidal.descLong: Paste a token from your device authorization flow.

ytdlp.title: The yt-dlp program
ytdlp.unknown: The newest version could not be looked up just now.
ytdlp.missing: Not installed — YouTube cannot play without it.
ytdlp.desc: YouTube offers no direct audio links, so every track is unlocked by this program. YouTube keeps changing how that works, and an out-of-date copy is the usual reason playback fails or sounds worse than it should.
ytdlp.shared: Shared by every YouTube and YouTube Music account on this server.

binary.title: The Soloist program
binary.expiring: Download a newer build and upload it here; that starts the 90 days again.
binary.accepts: Upload the .tar.gz as downloaded, or the unpacked soloist file.
binary.expired: This build has stopped working. Download a newer one and it is good for another 90 days.
binary.fetched: This server keeps it up to date — it checks daily and installs a new build when Spotify publishes one.
binary.fetching: Fetching it from Spotify now. This takes a moment the first time.
binary.manualOnly: Spotify publishes no build for {{arch}}, so this one has to be uploaded by hand.
binary.expiringSelf: A newer build arrives by itself well before then.

key.title: Your Soloist API key
key.desc: Create one in the Spotify developer dashboard with your Premium account.

lossless.title: Lossless
lossless.desc: Ask Spotify for lossless in every room. Off leaves it to Spotify, which picks a bitrate to suit the connection. Applies from the next track.

players.heading: Player

builtin.name: librespot
builtin.desc: The open-source Spotify client, built in and ready to use. Plays up to 320 kbps.
builtin.credentialsDesc: Spotify no longer accepts the logins this server can create on its own, so librespot needs credentials handed to it from the Spotify app once per account.

soloist.name: Spotify Soloist
soloist.desc: Spotify's own terminal client for headless setups. Supports lossless audio and also works with newer Spotify Premium accounts that no longer work with librespot.

players.roomsWaiting: Each room shows up in the Spotify app on its own. Pick one there once and it stays signed in.
players.roomsReady: Every room is signed in and shows up in the Spotify app.
players.roomsDesc: Soloist gets its credentials over Zeroconf: each room appears in your Spotify app by itself. Connect to it there once and its credentials are stored — after that it stays signed in.

subtitles.updates: Installed vs latest versions for core services. External checks are opt-in.

pairing.descPaired: This server is paired with a Loxone Miniserver. The Miniserver pushes the audio configuration and controls playback state for connected zones.

auth.desc: Require a login for the admin interface and the player. Credentials are checked against the Miniserver, so this only applies once paired.

groups.rowDesc: Let zones with different output protocols share a group. They play together, but without sample-accurate sync.
groups.note: A group still prefers protocol-based sync wherever it can — mixed groups only kick in when members cannot match.

tts.openaiApiKeyDesc: Needed by paid cloud services. Servers on your own network usually need nothing here.
tts.openaiModelDesc: Which voice model to ask for. Empty uses tts-1, which most servers accept.
tts.openaiVoiceDesc: Name of the voice, as your server calls it. Empty uses alloy.
tts.openaiFormatDesc: The format announcements are delivered in. mp3 works everywhere.

tts.validationOpenAi: Enter the server address, starting with http:// or https://.

zones.title: Zones
zones.subtitle: A zone is a single device you play music on. Group several to play in sync, and let phones and apps cast to one over AirPlay, Spotify Connect or DLNA — even devices that don't support those themselves.

setup.title: How are zones set up?
setup.desc: Pick one. You can change it later.

none.label: Disabled
none.desc: No zones. This server only shares your music with other apps through Access.

manual.label: Set up here
manual.desc: You add zones yourself — the speakers and rooms you name, group and cast to.

loxone.label: Loxone integrated
loxone.desc: Your Miniserver pushes which zones exist and their names — you still set each one's output and receivers here.

setup.confirmManualMessage: This disconnects the Loxone integration. The Miniserver stops supplying zones and you manage them here.
setup.confirmOffMessage: This disconnects the Loxone integration and leaves the server sharing content only.

loxone.modalPairedSub: Connected. Your Miniserver supplies the zones and their names; you configure each one's output and receivers here. Disconnect to manage zones locally instead.

loxone.step3: Deploy the changes and reboot the Miniserver to start pairing.

eqTitle.warn: EQ forwarder selected but no callback URL set

modal.resetVolumeCopy: Restore the configured default volume immediately when the zone is paused (matches the reference Loxone Audio Server).
modal.stateControllerDesc: Select where zone playback state is controlled.

eq.builtinDetail: Bakes the 10-band EQ into the ffmpeg pipeline on this audioserver, applied after resampling. Bands map onto ISO frequencies (31 Hz — 16 kHz) at Q 1. Slider changes restart the encoder, so expect a brief gap (<1 s) in audio while you adjust. Sync-group members follow the leader's EQ.
eq.squeezeliteIntro: Forwarder for the LoxBerry <1>Squeezelite Multi-Room</1> plugin. On every App-driven EQ write the audioserver POSTs <3>{ zoneId, bands }</3> to the plugin endpoint, which applies the 10-band values to the matching zone's alsaequal chain.
eq.callbackHelp: Point this at your LoxBerry host. Leave blank to keep the provider selected without forwarding — the chip on the tile turns amber to signal a missing URL.

output.typeDesc: Pick where this zone should play.
output.airplayBufferHint: Device read-ahead buffer. Default 750; raise (e.g. 1500) if this device stutters. Range 250–5000.
output.noTransports: No transports available for this build.
output.selectDevice: Select a device to route audio.
output.noCast: No Google Cast devices found yet.
output.probeTitle: Probe a Cast device by IP

output.manualError: Enter a Cast IP address to continue.

output.dlnaQualityDesc: Automatic asks the speaker which formats it accepts. Pick MP3 if the speaker stays silent or stutters, or Lossless to always send full quality.
output.maDesc: Pick the MA player that should act as this zone's output. Audio will play directly on that player; this server only proxies commands and mirrors state.
output.noMa: No Music Assistant players found on this bridge.
output.noMaBridge: No Music Assistant bridge configured. Add one under Content first.
output.maSourceMode: The selected Music Assistant bridge is in source mode. Switch it to sink mode under Content to use it as a zone output.

output.maDisabledTooltip: No Music Assistant bridge in sink mode. Configure one under Content first.
output.sendspinCopy: Build a synced speaker group: one leader is the reference, satellites are delayed to align.
output.sendspinSatellitesCopy: Extra listen-only clients fed the same audio, time-synced (e.g. a subwoofer or visualizer).
output.satelliteLatency: Per-speaker delay (ms) to align with the leader
output.mainDelayHint: Delay (ms) for the main speaker — applied live, no restart

output.snapcastCopy: Tap a client to map it to this zone.

power.sharedSubtitle: Use this only when multiple zones depend on the same power relay or supply.
power.editGroupSub: This updates the global group used by linked zones.
power.localSubtitle: Keep zone-specific wake-up timing here, plus any optional local trigger. The timing below also applies to speakers that switch themselves on, such as active speakers with line sensing.
power.preDelayHelp: Silence added before playback starts, so the speaker is awake before the first sound. Skipped while the zone counts as still on (see the standby timeout).
power.offDelayHelp: How long the zone counts as still on after playback stops. Within this window the wake-up delay is skipped. With a relay this is also when it switches off; with self-switching speakers, match it to how long they stay awake.

descriptions.gpio: Toggle a local GPIO line via gpioset using gpiochip + line offset.
descriptions.udp: Send ON/OFF payloads to a UDP endpoint.
descriptions.crelay: Switch a CRelay channel. Serial is optional when only one board is connected.

gpio.example: Example on Raspberry Pi 4: GPIO22 usually means chip <1>gpiochip0</1> and line offset <3>22</3>, not the old sysfs global number.

power.noLocal: No local relay configured. The wake-up delay and standby timeout above still apply, which is what active speakers with line sensing need.
power.name: Name

feedback.powerGroupsFailedDefault: Failed to update shared power groups: {{error}}

beoremote.title: Bang & Olufsen remote
beoremote.copy: Its keys drive this room. Each model is switched on separately.
beoremote.submenuCopy: One source can open a second list. Pick what goes in it.
beoremote.lineInsTitle: Turntable, CD player and other inputs
beoremote.lineInsCopy: Show devices plugged into this server as sources on the remote.
beoremote.keysCopy: Each button starts something in this room. On Default it plays the favourite it lines up with.
beoremote.keysFailed: Could not load the buttons for this room. Try reopening this screen.
beoremote.keyDefaultEmpty: No favourite in this position yet
beoremote.useTitle: Use a Bang & Olufsen remote here
beoremote.deviceCopy: Which device's remote drives this room. It follows the speaker unless you pick another; pairing happens on whichever it is.
beoremote.pairCopy: Press this, then put the remote into pairing mode.
beoremote.essenceButtons: Play and pause, skip forward and back, volume and mute — five fixed buttons and a wheel, so there is nothing to set. Pair it and it works.
beoremote.pairCopyEssence: Press this, then hold the power button on the remote until a green light blinks.

bluetooth.useCopy: Let a phone pair with this room's speaker and play to it.
bluetooth.deviceCopy: Which device's radio this room uses. It follows the speaker unless you pick another; pairing happens on whichever it is.
bluetooth.windowCopy: How long the speaker is visible after the pairing button is pressed.
bluetooth.pinCopy: For phones that ask for one. Most pair with a confirmation instead.
bluetooth.controlTitle: Let the phone control the room
bluetooth.controlCopy: Its play, pause and skip keys, and the track it shows.
bluetooth.pairCopy: Opens the window, then look for the room on the phone.
bluetooth.pairOpen: Findable now as “{{name}}” — pick it on the phone.
bluetooth.noPhones: No phone has been paired with this room yet.

device.cardCopy: The output the speaker is wired to.
device.cardDefault: Whatever the device uses by default
device.volumeCopy: Where the speaker turns it down. Its own sound card is best when it has a volume of its own — doing it in software throws away detail the speaker would have kept.
device.volumeAuto: The sound card, if it has volume

access.title: How this server connects
access.subtitle: Share the content you set up with other apps and devices on your network, and send what is playing to your home automation — all through one server. Turn on what you need; each works on its own.

servers.failedMessage: Failed to update the server settings
servers.subsonicNoCredentials: Create a user under Users first — this server has no Miniserver to authenticate against.

dlna.name: DLNA / UPnP
dlna.purpose: A media server on your network: any DLNA device — smart TV, receiver, speaker — browses and plays everything this server offers. Streaming services included, so Spotify or Apple Music reach gear that has no app for them.

subsonic.name: Subsonic API
subsonic.purpose: A widely supported music API. Point an app like Symfonium, Amperfy or DSub at the address below and sign in with your account to browse and stream everything this server offers.

loxone.name: Loxone Audio Server
loxone.purpose: A complete Loxone Audioserver implementation: it integrates fully into your Loxone setup and behaves like the real thing.
loxone.hint: Switch this on under Players, by choosing Loxone integrated.

webdav.name: Network drive
webdav.purpose: Adds the music folder to your computer as a network drive, so you can drag albums in and organise them with Finder or Explorer. Connect to the address below and sign in with your account. New files are picked up automatically.

mqtt.name: Home automation (MQTT)
mqtt.purpose: Sends what each zone is playing to an MQTT broker, and takes instructions back the same way — so home automation can show what is on and control it without asking this server over and over.
mqtt.brokerDesc: The address of your MQTT broker, and the port if it is not the usual 1883.
mqtt.authDesc: Leave both empty if your broker accepts connections without a password.
mqtt.prefixDesc: Everything is published under this name. Change it if another server already uses it on the same broker.
mqtt.topicDesc: Each zone is published at {{prefix}}/zones/<zone number>, both as one message with everything in it and as separate values you can read one at a time. To control a zone, publish to that same address with /set/volume, /set/state and so on.
mqtt.progressDesc: Keeps a live counter of how far into the track each zone is. Off by default because it sends a message every second per zone; everything else is sent only when it changes.
mqtt.disconnected: Not connected to the broker yet.
mqtt.hostRequired: Fill in the broker address before switching this on.
mqtt.dialogSubtitle: Where to publish and listen, and how to sign in.
mqtt.controlNote: Anyone who can publish to your broker can control this server, just as anyone who can read it can see what is playing. Use your broker's own accounts and permissions to decide who that is.

sonnClients.saved: Saved. The device picks this up within a few seconds.
sonnClients.forgetMessage: {{name}} disappears from this list. Its settings are deleted; the device itself keeps running and will register again unless you switch it off.
sonnClients.deviceNameDesc: Overrides the hostname the box registered under. It is also the name a speaker on this box appears under when you pick a room's output.
sonnClients.emptyBody: Run this on any Raspberry Pi you want to bring into the system. It turns the machine into an appliance: it finds this server by itself, shows up here, and then you choose what it does.

players.title: Speakers
players.desc: One per sound card. Each one becomes an output you can assign to a room on the Zones screen.
players.empty: No speaker set up yet. Add one and pick the sound card it is wired to.
players.noCards: This device has not reported any sound cards yet.
players.cardDesc: The output the speaker is wired to.
players.volumeControlDesc: Where the speaker turns the volume down. Its own sound card is best when it has a volume of its own — turning it down in software throws away detail the speaker would have kept.
players.volumeAuto: The sound card, if it has volume
players.volumeScaleDesc: How a percentage lands on the speaker's own volume. Spread by loudness suits most speakers; one that shows its own number — a Bang & Olufsen on 0-90, say — is better on its own scale, so the two match.
players.volumeHookDesc: For a speaker with its own volume control. Leave empty to let the device do the volume itself.
players.removeDesc: The device stops playing through this card. Nothing on the device itself changes.
players.removeInUse: {{room}} plays through this speaker. Give that room another output first, or it goes quiet.

version.hint: Each speaker installs it on its next check-in, never mid-song, and puts its previous version back by itself if it will not start.
version.published: Speakers will move to {{version}} once they are idle.
version.notPublished: There is no published build for {{version}}.

sources.title: Inputs
sources.desc: A turntable, CD player or anything else plugged into this device. It becomes a source you can play in any room.
sources.noCards: This device has not reported any inputs yet.
sources.cardDesc: The socket the equipment is plugged into.
sources.controlHookDesc: Runs on the device to switch the equipment on and pass play, pause and skip to it.
sources.configuredOnLineIn: Silence detection and the capture format are set there too.
sources.removeDesc: Nothing on the device itself changes; the socket simply stops being offered as a source.
sources.removeInUse: The “{{name}}” line-in plays this input. Remove that line-in first, or it falls silent.

remote.title: Beoremote One
remote.desc: Show your own sources on a Bang & Olufsen remote paired to this device.
remote.label: Remote
remote.volumePlayerDesc: Which speaker on this device the volume buttons change.
remote.pairingStarted: Put the remote into pairing mode now. It has 90 seconds.
remote.assignOnZone: Pairing a remote, and what its screen lists, are set on the room it drives — under Zones, beside the speaker it plays through.

errors.generic: That did not save. Try again.
errors.deviceInUse: Still in use by a room: {{ids}}. Change that room's speaker first.
errors.duplicate-client-id: Two speakers cannot share one id.
errors.beoremote-missing-zone: Pick the room the remote should control.
errors.player-missing-client-id: A speaker is missing its id.
errors.source-missing-client-id: An input is missing its id.

sonnClients.emptyHint: A device can play music in a room, listen to a turntable or CD player, take a phone over Bluetooth, and drive a Beoremote One. All four are optional and independent — a Pi at the record player needs no speaker of its own, and the room it plays in can be a different box entirely.
sonnClients.addBody: Run this on the next Raspberry Pi. It finds this server by itself and shows up here.

tile.behind: An update is available for this device.

standing.bareDetail: Add the speaker it is wired to

usage.noRoom: Not used by a room yet
usage.noLineIn: Not used by a line-in yet
usage.sourceLineInNote: This input feeds the “{{name}}” line-in, so it can be played in any room. Line-ins live on the Content screen.
usage.sourceFreeNote: Nothing plays this input yet. Add a line-in on the Content screen and point it at this id:

cards.default: Whatever the device uses by default

bluetooth.title: Bluetooth
bluetooth.desc: A phone plays straight into the room over the air, and its own buttons steer what it started. Both are set up beside the room's speaker, on the Zones screen.

about.title: What this device is
about.idHint: The device's own id, as it registered itself:

room.title: Room
room.standaloneDesc: Wire up what it does one at a time — for a box serving two rooms, or one at a turntable whose input any room can play.
room.claimedDesc: It plays this room, a phone pairs with this room, and its remote drives it. Set once here instead of three times on the room.

log.title: Log
log.noAnswer: The speaker did not send its log. It may be offline.

claim.title: Not claimed yet
claim.detail: This speaker can see more than one server. Claim it to use it here.
claim.sees: It can see {{servers}}. Claim it to use it here.

move.title: Move this speaker?
move.message: {{name}} stops being this server’s. It offers itself to every server on the network again, and you claim it on the one you want.
